chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was ill on three occasions; in each illness he would make a will, and when he recovered he would confirm/execute his will.

key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn, the fourth Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a will made during illness if the person recovers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the prophetic tradition of Imam Zayn al-Abidin, illustrating that a will drafted during temporary illness remains valid and binding upon recovery, thereby preventing the need for re-drafting. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the testator's intent, once clearly expressed during a period of health or specific illness, is not invalidated by subsequent recovery, ensuring the stability of estate distribution.
